author: Augustine of Hippo
occasion: The text does not explicitly state the occasion. Augustine offers an exposition of the baptismal creed to guard new believers against heretical distortions.
argument: Augustine explains the articles of the creed in order, beginning with God the Father almighty as creator of all things from nothing. He then treats the eternal generation of the Son, the incarnation, crucifixion, resurrection, ascension, and future judgment. He defends the full divinity and co-equality of the Holy Spirit within the one divine substance. Finally he expounds the church, forgiveness of sins, and the resurrection of the body, urging that faith must be held before it can be understood.

outline.move: Augustine states the need to profess the faith aloud and explains why the creed is a brief rule for beginners.
He argues that God the Father is almighty because he created all things from nothing, even any underlying matter.
He explains that the Son is the eternal Word and Wisdom of the Father, begotten not made, equal to the Father.
He distinguishes the Son's eternal generation from his temporal creation as man, the humble way by which we return to God.
He argues that since God is the one who truly is, nothing can be contrary to him except what is not.
He defends the full humanity of Christ's birth from the Virgin Mary, his crucifixion under Pontius Pilate, and his burial.
He treats the resurrection, ascension, session at the Father's right hand, and coming judgment.
He expounds the Holy Spirit as consubstantial and co-eternal with the Father and the Son, and discusses how the three are one God.
He explains belief in the holy catholic church and the forgiveness of sins.
He expounds the resurrection of the body, arguing that the flesh will be changed into a spiritual body.
He concludes that the creed is a brief rule to be held by faith, lived rightly, and then understood.

key_terms.sense: The baptismal creed, a brief rule of faith handed to new Christians
God's attribute as creator of all things from nothing
The eternal Word of God, the Son, through whom all things were made
The Son as the only-begotten of the Father, not made
Christ as firstborn among many adopted brothers and sisters
God's saving plan carried out in time through Christ's incarnation, death, and resurrection
Human flesh, especially the visible body that will be raised and changed
The highest part of the human person, the rational mind, or the Holy Spirit depending on context
The soul, the life that joins spirit to body
The one God in three persons, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit
The underlying reality or essence of God, shared by the three persons
The universal church united in love of God and neighbor
The forgiveness of sins granted by God
The future rising of the visible flesh, changed into a spiritual body
Love, especially the love of God poured into hearts by the Holy Spirit

scripture: Augustine uses Old Latin versions of the Bible, with Psalms numbered according to the Septuagint. Modern citations should use standard English Bible book names and, for Psalms, the Hebrew numbering with a note where the Septuagint numbering differs.
uncertain: The exact date of composition is inferred from Augustine's early career; the text itself does not state a date.
The precise occasion and addressee are not stated in the text.
Whether Augustine endorses or merely reports the view that the Holy Spirit is the mutual love of Father and Son is left open in section 20.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Paul ... source_forms: ["Paulus apostolus", "apostolus"] ... 'The apostle explicitly named in section 23; elsewhere Augustine cites 'the apostle' without always specifying which one.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: section 1: 'ait enim apostolus: corde creditur ad iustitiam, ore autem confessio fit ad salutem'; section 5: 'quia et apostolus dicit: qui cum in forma dei esset constitutus'; section 13: 'sicut ad sinistram haedi constituuntur'; section 14: 'in quo exsecratur apostolus eos, qui commutauerunt gloriam incorruptibilis dei in similitudinem corruptibilis hominis'; section 15: 'secundum auctoritatem, quae apostolorum actibus continetur'; section 18: 'tractantur haec latius ab eis'; section 21: 'sicut apostolica disciplina commendat'; section 23: 'de quo dicit apostolus: mente seruio legi dei, qui item alio loco dicit: testis est enim mihi deus, cui seruio in spiritu meo'
_unresolved_facts.fix: Paul is explicitly named as 'Paulus apostolus' only in section 24 ('uidetur enim Paulus apostolus eam tamquam digito ostendere'), not section 23. In section 23, 'apostolus' is cited twice without the name Paulus. The claim that Paul is 'explicitly named in section 23' is wrong; he is named in section 24. Also, 'apostolus' in sections 1, 5, 13, 14, 21, 23 refers to Paul, but section 15's 'apostolorum actibus' refers to Acts of the Apostles, not Paul's voice. The source_forms should not include bare 'apostolus' without qualification, as it is ambiguous.

_unresolved_facts.claim: John ... source_forms: ["Iohannes apostolus"] ... 'The apostle cited in section 19 for the statement 'God is love.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: section 19: 'huc accedit aliud testimonium, quod dicit Iohannes apostolus, quoniam deus dilectio est'
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source has 'Iohannes apostolus' but the brief's claim that this is 'for the statement 'God is love'' is slightly misleading because the Latin reads 'deus dilectio est' not 'God is love' (caritas/dilectio distinction). More importantly, the brief misses that John is also cited in section 1 implicitly? No—checking: section 1 quotes 'nisi credideritis, non intellegetis' which is Isaiah 7:9. The John citation is only in section 19. However, the source_forms should note that 'Iohannes' appears without 'apostolus' in the text? No, it has 'Iohannes apostolus'. This is minor. Actually the real issue: the brief says 'God is love' but Augustine quotes 'deus dilectio est' and discusses this exact wording. The brief's English rendering 'God is love' is conventional but not the precise source wording. This is acceptable as a translation issue, not factual. Withdraw this as not a real problem.

_unresolved_facts.source_quote: section 15: 'ex hac itaque temporali dispensatione loquitur in Apocalypsi, ubi scriptum est: haec dicit qui est et qui fuit et qui uenturus est'
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source has 'Apocalypsi' (dative/ablative), not 'Apocalypsis' (nominative). The brief's nominative form 'Apocalypsis' does not match the source form. Correct to 'Apocalypsi' or note the source form.

_unresolved_facts.claim: sections ["8", "9", "10", "11"]: 'He defends the full humanity of Christ's birth from the Virgin Mary, his crucifixion under Pontius Pilate, and his burial.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: section 9: 'Detestandi autem etiam illi sunt, qui dominum nostrum Iesum Christum matrem Mariam in terris negant habuisse'
_unresolved_facts.fix: Section 9 does not defend Christ's 'birth from the Virgin Mary' directly; rather, it defends that Mary was Christ's mother on earth against those who deny it, and interprets difficult sayings of Jesus about his mother. The birth from the Virgin is treated in section 8 ('natus est per spiritum sanctum ex uirgine Maria'). Section 9's focus is on Mary's motherhood and Jesus' words, not the virgin birth per se. Adjust to: 'He defends the virgin birth (8), Mary's motherhood and Jesus' sayings about her (9), the purity of the incarnation against objections (10), and the crucifixion under Pontius Pilate and burial (11).'

_unresolved_facts.claim: sections ["16", "17", "18", "19", "20"]: 'He expounds the Holy Spirit as consubstantial and co-eternal with the Father and the Son, and discusses how the three are one God.'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: section 18: entire section discusses the Father and Son, not the Holy Spirit; 'Et de patre quidem ac filio multis libris disseruerunt docti et spiritales uiri'
_unresolved_facts.fix: Section 18 does not expound the Holy Spirit; it discusses the Father and Son relationship, addressing heretical misinterpretations of scriptural passages about Christ's subordination. The Holy Spirit is not mentioned in section 18. Adjust sections to [16, 17, 19, 20] for Holy Spirit exposition, with 18 treated separately as 'He addresses scriptural passages about the Son's relation to the Father and refutes heretical interpretations of Christ's subordination.'
